spots.name: Tsitsernakaberd
spots.summary: The Armenian Genocide Memorial complex is Armenia's official memorial dedicated to the victims of the Armenian genocide, built in 1967 on the hill of Tsitsernakaberd in Yerevan.

names.ja: ツィツェルナカベルト
names.zh: 亞美尼亞種族滅絕博物館

spots.name: Republic Square
spots.summary: Republic Square is the central town square in Yerevan, the capital of Armenia. It consists of two sections: an oval roundabout and a trapezoid-shaped section which contains a pool with musical fountains.

spots.name: Blue Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Blue Mosque is an 18th-century Iranian Twelver Shia mosque, located in Yerevan, Armenia. It was commissioned by Hoseyn Ali Khan, the khan of the Erivan Khanate. It is one of the oldest extant structures in central Yerevan and the most significant structure from the city's Iranian period.

spots.name: Mother Armenia
spots.summary: Mother Armenia is a female personification of Armenia. Her most public visual rendering is a monumental statue in Victory Park overlooking the capital city of Yerevan, Armenia.

spots.name: Saint Gregory the Illuminator Cathedral

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Saint Gregory the Illuminator Cathedral, also known as the Yerevan Cathedral, is the largest cathedral of the Armenian Apostolic Church.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Saint Gregory the Illuminator Cathedral, Yerevan

names.nl: Saint Gregory the Illuminator Cathedral, Yerevan

spots.name: National Gallery of Armenia

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The National Gallery of Armenia is the largest fine arts museum in Armenia. Located on Yerevan's Republic Square, the museum has one of the most prominent locations in the Armenian capital.

names.ja: アルメニア国立美術館

spots.name: Erebuni Fortress
spots.summary: Erebuni Fortress is an Urartian fortified city, located in Yerevan, Armenia. It is 1,017 metres (3,337 ft) above sea level. It was one of several fortresses built along the northern Urartian border and was one of the most important political, economic and cultural centers of the vast kingdom.

spots.name: History Museum of Armenia

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The History Museum of Armenia is a museum in Armenia with departments of Archaeology, Numismatics, Ethnography, Modern History and Restoration. It has a national collection of 400,000 objects and was founded in 1920.

names.ja: アルメニア歴史博物館

spots.name: Matenadaran

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sun

spots.summary: The Matenadaran, officially the Mesrop Mashtots Institute of Ancient Manuscripts, is the largest center for the storage, study and popularization of Armenian manuscripts, combining the functions of a museum, archive and scientific institution. It holds the most extensive collection of Armenian manuscripts in existence.

spots.name: Karen Demirchyan Complex

hours.note: Closed Sat, Sun

spots.summary: Karen Demirchyan Sports and Concerts Complex, also known as Demirchyan Arena, Sports & Music Complex, or simply Hamalir, is a large multi-purpose sports and concert complex with 184 stairs leading up Tsitsernakaberd hill which dominates over the western parts of Yerevan, near the Hrazdan River gorge.

names.ja: カレン・デミルチャン・コンプレックス
names.zh: 凱倫·德米徹恩體育和音樂會綜合大樓

spots.name: Katoghike Church, Yerevan

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Katoghike Holy Mother of God Church is a small medieval church in the Kentron District of Yerevan, the capital of Armenia.

spots.name: Yerevan Opera Theatre
spots.summary: The Alexander Spendiaryan National Academic Opera and Ballet Theatre, simply known by locals as 'Opera', is an opera theatre in Yerevan. It officially opened on 20 January 1933, with a performance of Alexander Spendiaryan's opera Almast; the venue is named after this composer.

names.ru: Армянский академический театр оперы и балета им. А. Спендиарова
names.ja: エレバン・オペラ劇場

spots.name: Saint Sarkis Cathedral

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Saint Sarkis Cathedral is an Armenian cathedral in Yerevan, Armenia. It is the seat of the Araratian Pontifical Diocese of the Armenian Apostolic Church. It was built in 1842, on the left bank of the Hrazdan River in Yerevan's Kentron District.

spots.name: Yerevan 2800th Anniversary Park
spots.summary: Yerevan 2800th Anniversary Park, also known as the Vardanyans' park, was opened on 10 May 2019. The park is a gift from philanthropists Mikayel and Karen Vardanyan on the 2800th anniversary of the foundation of Yerevan city.

names.zh: 葉里溫建城2800周年紀念公園

spots.name: Northern Avenue
spots.summary: Northern Avenue is a pedestrian avenue in Yerevan, Armenia, opened in 2007. It is in the central Kentron district and links Abovyan Street with Freedom Square on Tumanyan street. It is 450 metres (1,480 ft) long and 27 metres (89 ft) wide.

spots.name: Komitas Pantheon
spots.summary: Komitas Park and Pantheon is located in Yerevan's Shengavit District, on the right side of the main Arshakunyats Avenue, in Armenia. It was formed in 1936 after the demolition of the Mler cemetery and its historic chapel.

names.ja: コミタス・パンテオン

spots.name: Surp Anna Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Saint Anna Church is an Armenian Apostolic Church opened in 2015 in the Kentron District of Yerevan, Armenia, adjacent to the 13th-century Katoghike Church.

spots.name: Victory Park
spots.summary: Victory Park, is a public park located in the Kanaker-Zeytun District of Yerevan, the capital of Armenia.

spots.name: David of Sassoun
spots.summary: David of Sassoun is a copper equestrian statue portraying David of Sassoun in Yerevan, Armenia. Erected by the sculptor and artist Yervand Kochar in 1959, it depicts the protagonist of the Armenian national epic Daredevils of Sassoun. It is placed on a basalt base shaped to resemble natural rock formations.

spots.name: Freedom Square
spots.summary: The Freedom Square or Liberty Square, also known as Opera Square and, formerly, Theatre Square until 1991, is a town square located in Kentron (Center) district of Yerevan, Armenia.

spots.name: Zoravor Surp Astvatsatsin Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Zoravor Surp Astvatsatsin Church is the second oldest surviving church in Yerevan. It was previously known as Surp Astvatsatsin. However, the name Zoravor was added because the church was home to the 13th century bible of Zoravor.

spots.name: Sergei Parajanov Museum
spots.summary: The Sergei Parajanov Museum is a tribute to Soviet Armenian film director and artist Sergei Parajanov and is one of the most popular museums in Yerevan. It represents Parajanov's diverse artistic and literary heritage.

names.zh: 谢尔盖·帕拉杰诺夫博物馆

spots.name: Saint John the Baptist Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Saint John the Baptist Church is an active church in the old area of Kond, Yerevan, Armenia. First, it was built on the height of Kond district, in 1710, in the place of a medieval church ruined as the result of a 1689 earthquake. It was built by a rich man, Melik Aghamal, living in Yerevan.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Saint John the Baptist Church, Yerevan

names.zh: 聖約翰施洗者教堂 (葉里溫)

spots.name: English Park
spots.summary: The English Park is a public park in Yerevan, Armenia, located on Italy Street. It occupies an area of 5.5 hectares in the central Kentron district of the city, just to the south of the Republic Square.

spots.name: Yerevan TV Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Yerevan TV Tower is a 311.7-metre (1,023 ft) high lattice tower built in 1977 on Nork Hill near downtown Yerevan, Armenia. It is the tallest structure in Armenia, fourth-tallest tower in Western Asia, sixth-tallest free-standing lattice tower and thirty-eighth-tallest tower in the world.

spots.name: Aram Street
spots.summary: Aram Street, is a street at the central Kentron district of the Armenian capital Yerevan, named after Aram Manukian; the leader of the Van Resistance of 1915 and one of the founders of the First Republic of Armenia. It is one of the oldest streets in modern Yerevan.

spots.name: Moscow Cinema
spots.summary: Moscow Cinema is a cinema hall in the Armenian capital Yerevan. It is located in Charles Aznavour Square on Abovyan Street.

spots.name: Abovyan Street
spots.summary: Abovyan Street, is a street at the central Kentron district of the Armenian capital Yerevan. It was known as Astafyan Street between 1868 and 1920.

spots.name: Erivan Fortress
spots.summary: Erivan Fortress or Yerevan Fortress was a 16th-century fortress in Yerevan.

spots.name: Baghramyan Avenue
spots.summary: Marshal Baghramyan Avenue is an avenue in the central Kentron and the northwestern Arabkir districts of Yerevan, Armenia. The avenue is named after the Soviet Armenian commander and Marshal of the Soviet Union Hovhannes Baghramyan whose statue stands at the central part of the avenue.

spots.name: Red Bridge
spots.summary: The Red Bridge is a 17th-century bridge built of red tuff on the Hrazdan River in Yerevan, Armenia. An earlier bridge in the same place was ruined by the 1679 Armenia earthquake.

spots.name: Yerablur
spots.summary: Yerablur or Yerablur Military Pantheon is a military cemetery located on a hilltop in the outskirts of Yerevan, Armenia. Since 1988, Yerablur has become the burial place of Armenian soldiers who died during the Nagorno-Karabakh conflict.

spots.name: Tamanyan Street
spots.summary: Tamanyan Street is a pedestrian street in Yerevan, Armenia. It is located in the central Kentron district and links the Yerevan Cascade at the north with the Moscow street at the south. It has a length of 200 metres (660 ft) and a width of 55 metres (180 ft).

spots.name: Charents Museum of Literature and Arts

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Charents Museum of Literature and Arts is the largest repository of Armenian manuscripts and books encompassing the last three hundred years, located in Yerevan, Armenia.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Charents Museum of Literature and Arts

names.fr: Musée d'art et de littérature Yéghiché Tcharents
names.es: Museo de Literatura y Artes Yeghishe Charents
names.ru: Музей литературы и искусства имени Егише Чаренца
names.ja: チャレンツ文学芸術博物館
names.zh: 夏伦特文学和艺术博物馆

spots.name: Circular Park
spots.summary: The Circular Park ; also known as the Youth Park, is a public park in the Kentron district of the Armenian capital Yerevan. It starts with the Cathedral of Saint Gregory at the south on Tigran Mets street, and ends up with the Poplavok lake at the north near Mashtots Avenue.

spots.name: National Library of Armenia
spots.summary: The National Library of Armenia is a national public library in Yerevan, Armenia. It was founded in 1832 as part of the state gymnasium-school of Yerevan. During the Soviet era, from 1925 to 1990, it was named after the Armenian Bolshevik revolutionary and statesman Alexander Miasnikian.

names.ja: アルメニア国立図書館

spots.name: Yerevan Zoo
spots.summary: The Yerevan Zoo, also known as the Zoological Park of Yerevan, is a zoological park in Yerevan, the capital of Armenia, that was founded in 1940 and is the only one in the country. It is located in the southeastern part of the city, at the foot of the hills, covering an area of 35 hectares.

spots.name: Charles Aznavour Square
spots.summary: Charles Aznavour Square is a small square in the Kentron District of the Armenian capital Yerevan. The square is named in honour of the French Armenian singer Charles Aznavour as part of the celebrations of the 10th anniversary of Armenian independence in 2001.

spots.name: Mashtots Avenue
spots.summary: Mashtots Avenue, known as Lenin Avenue until 1990, is an avenue in the central Kentron district of Yerevan, Armenia.

spots.name: Erebuni Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Erebuni Historical-Archaeological Reserve-Museum, was established on October 19, 1968. The opening of the museum was timed to coincide with the 2750th anniversary of Yerevan. The Museum stands at the foot of the Arin Berd hill, on top of which the Urartian Fortress Erebouni has stood since 782 BCE.

spots.name: Cathedral of Avan

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Cathedral of Avan is a ruined late 6th-century church located in the Avan District of Yerevan, the capital of Armenia. It is the oldest surviving church inside Yerevan's city limits, and earliest dated example of tetraconch church.

spots.name: Zalkhan Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Zalkhan Mosque, also sometimes called Zal khan Mosque or Sheher Mosque, was a Twelver Shia mosque, located in the Shahar quarter of Yerevan, in what is modern-day Armenia. The mosque was built in c. 1687 in what was then Iran, and is believed to have been demolished in 1926.

spots.name: Lovers' Park
spots.summary: Lovers' Park is a public park in Yerevan, Armenia, located on Baghramyan Avenue. It occupies an area of 2.5 hectares in the central Kentron District of the city.

spots.name: National Assembly Building of Armenia
spots.summary: The National Assembly Building of Armenia is the home of the National Assembly of Armenia. The building is located on Baghramyan Avenue in Yerevan, Armenia's capital city. It was designed by Mark Grigorian. It was completed in 1950 and initially housed the legislature of Soviet Armenia, the Supreme Soviet.

spots.name: Aznavour Centre

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Aznavour Centre is Aznavour Foundation's first cultural project. The French President Emmanuel Macron and the Armenian President Armen Sarkissian were present at the Aznavour Centre project presentation.

spots.name: Haghtanak bridge
spots.summary: The Victory Bridge or Haghtanak Bridge is an arch bridge for traffic linking across the Hrazdan River in Yerevan, Armenia. It connects the Mashtots Avenue in the east with the Admiral Isakov Avenue in the west.

spots.name: The Men
spots.summary: The Men is a public artwork in Yerevan, the capital of Armenia. Created by Armenian sculptor Davit Minasyan in 2007, it commemorates Edmond Keosayan's 1972 film of the same name, and comprises four statues, depicting the film's stars, the actors Mher Mkrtchyan, Avetik Gevorkyan, Armen Ayvazyan, and Azat Sherents.

spots.name: Holy Trinity Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Holy Trinity Church is an Armenian Apostolic Church constructed in 2003 in the Malatia-Sebastia District of Yerevan, Armenia. It is modeled after the 7th century Zvartnots Cathedral.

spots.name: St. Paul and Peter Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Saint Paul and Peter Church was an Armenian Apostolic church in Yerevan, Armenia originally built during the 5th-6th centuries. It was demolished in November 1930 to make room for the Moscow Cinema on Abovyan Street.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Saints Peter and Paul Church, Yerevan

spots.name: Mordechai Navi Synagogue

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Mordechai Navi Synagogue, also called the Mordechai Navi Jewish Centre, is a Jewish congregation and synagogue, located at 23 Nar Dos Street, in the central Kentron district of Yerevan, the capital of Armenia. The synagogue was opened in June 2011.

spots.name: Saint Hakob Church of Kanaker

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Surp Hakob Church is located in the Kanaker-Zeytun District within the city limits of Yerevan, the capital of Armenia. Its sister-church, Surp Astvatsatsin, is located upon a hilltop to the northwest within sight of the Church of S. Hakob.

spots.name: Sayat-Nova Avenue
spots.summary: Sayat-Nova Avenue, is an avenue in the central Kentron District of Yerevan, Armenia. It is named after the 18th-century Armenian poet and musician Sayat-Nova. It was officially inaugurated on 27 October 1963.

spots.name: Palace of Sardar

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Palace of Sardar or Sardar Palace is the former residence of Sardar, the ruler of the Erivan Khanate. It was located in the northeastern part of the Erivan Fortress in Yerevan, on the left bank of the Hrazdan river.

spots.name: Near East Art Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Near East Art Museum is a museum of art located in Yerevan, Armenia. The museum was opened in 1993 and is based on a collection donated by Marcos Grigorian, painter, collector and honorary citizen of Yerevan in memory of his daughter, actress Sabrina Grigorian.

names.es: Museo de Arte del Medio Oriente

spots.name: Armenian Railways Museum

hours.note: Closed Sat, Sun

spots.summary: The Armenian Railways Museum is a railway museum in Yerevan, Armenia.

names.fr: Musée arménien des chemins de fer

spots.name: Komitas Museum

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: Officially, Komitas Museum-Institute is an art and biographical museum in Yerevan, Armenia, devoted to the renowned Armenian musicologist and composer Komitas. It is located adjacent to the pantheon at the Komitas Park of Shengavit district. The museum was opened in January 2015.

spots.name: Yerevan History Museum

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: The Yerevan History Museum is the history museum of Yerevan, the capital city of Armenia. The museum was founded in 1931 as the Communal Museum. Currently, the museum is located in a building attached to the Yerevan City Hall. The architect of the building was Jim Torosyan.

spots.name: Saint Nikolai Cathedral, Yerevan

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Saint Nikolai Cathedral was a Russian Orthodox cathedral in Yerevan, Armenia. It was destroyed by Soviet forces in 1931. It was located at the site of what is now Shahumyan Square in Yerevan's Kentron District.

spots.name: Yeghishe Charents House-Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Yeghishe Charents House Museum, also known as the Yeghishe Charents Memorial Museum, is the house museum in Yerevan, Armenia where the poet Yeghishe Charents lived from 1935 to 1937.

spots.name: Teishebaini

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Teishebaini was the capital of the Transcaucasian provinces of the ancient kingdom of Urartu. It is located near the modern city of Yerevan in Armenia.

spots.name: Singing Fountains
spots.summary: The big fountains of Republic Square with a music, light and of course dancing water show every evening.

Cascades, Sculpture Park and Cafesjian Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Sculpture Park is a small green zone in the immediate North of the Opera. Sculptures from Botero and other artists of international fame decorate the park. The park is part of Cafesjian Museum - the Armenian version of Guggenheim. spots.name: Sunken Fountain
spots.summary: At the foot of the Cascade complex, which itself has many fountains, this sunken fountain with lots of seating is one of Yerevan's coolest spots to escape the heat of summer.

spots.name: Climb the Cascades

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: (or - before 20:00 - take the escalators inside the art gallery, stepping outside at each level) one evening for the great views of the city and Mt. Ararat, then head across the street to the amusement park inside Victory Park for some cotton candy and a ride on the rickety Ferris wheel.

spots.name: Opera park
spots.summary: Spend a late night at a café in the Opera park, and outside the Melody Café for some of the best people watching in Yerevan.

spots.name: Fountains of Saryan Post Park
spots.summary: Tons of fountains - including a huge splash pad that kids love to run through in the summer.

spots.name: Cafesjian Museum of Modern Art
spots.summary: A modern art museum, housing the collection of Gerard Cafesjian. It has Arshile Gorky, Andy Warhol, Marc Chagall and other big names on display. The collection is very rich in Glass Art, has many pieces of the Libenský-Brychtová couple, including specially made 'For Armenia' series. Special galleries display monumental tryptichons or reliefs focusing on Armenian history. Entry can be made at any l

spots.name: Museum of Woodwork

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Houses some artifacts of Armenian historical wood carving culture (doors, furniture and the like), and wood-based sculptures by modern day artists.

spots.name: Cascade Memorial to the Victims of Soviet Repression
spots.summary: Monument dedicated to the memory of the victims of Soviet-era murders and deportations, atop the Yerevan Cascade, next to the obelisk that commemorates 50 years of Soviet Armenia. The Cascade Memorial was designed by Jim Torosyan, Yerevan's chief architect between 1971 and 1981, and was constructed in the late 1980s and completed around 2008. Inside the large concrete structure, a memorial slab ha

spots.name: Yerevan City Hall
spots.summary: The city's administration is housed in this massive five-story building. Construction started during Soviet times, was halted in 1991 for over a decade and the building was finally completed in 2004. The Yerevan History Museum is attached to it.

spots.name: Abovian street
spots.summary: It's home to very few remaining Belle Époque period structures of Republican Armenia. Some gems of Art Nouveau, early Modern (constructivist and the like), and Moorish Revival style can be found in the backyards of Abovian, Nalbandian and Hanrapetutian streets. Most often they are in a very poor condition due to neglect. Hanrapetutian st. might get a special attention if you are not time constrain

spots.name: Artashi Mot

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Cheap shaurmas, soups and kebabs upstairs, fancier but still well priced sit-down restaurant underground. Great place to have BBQ and to meet your traditional fast food cravings. The fancier part is considered by many to be the finest place for khorovats (BBQ) in Armenia. Judge for yourself, but not before trying the horti (beef) and sunki (mushroom) barbeques. They are both delicious, when they h

spots.name: Grand Candy Ponchikanots
spots.summary: Ponchiks are a regional type of donut. Fried dough stuffed with a custard and topped with powdered sugar. Grand Candy took over the old space of a popular former Soviet "ponchikanots", or place of ponchiks and this is a popular spot for a fresh, hot, and very cheap treat. Lots of locally made candy and chocolate for sale as well. Grand Candy's big competition in the ponchik realm came down from Gy

spots.name: Lavash

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Very good menu of traditional Armenian cuisine. The large room upstairs is a more refined white-tablecloth experience, but prices are the same. Can be busy on weekend nights, reserve ahead. Absolutely end the meal with the famous millefeuille cake (layers of fillo and pastry custard); trying to save some space for it is a lost cause, however - the one-serving slab is enormous even for two (and som

spots.name: Tavern Yerevan

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The place for traditional Armenian cuisine. You'll have to rub shoulders with an occasional government function, a wedding shower or a busful of tourists, but the food is the real thing. Do not be scared by the names of the dishes - the more unpronounceable, the tastier (tzhvzhik, for example, is fegata alla veneziana, offal with fried onions - delicious!), and the English menu has helpful descrip

spots.name: Tumanyan Khinkali

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Khinkali (sturdy soup dumplings, similar to xiao long bao that came to Caucasus over the Silk Road) with meat or cheese filling is the name of the game here. You can have them boiled or fried; they are priced per dumpling, and 6-8 should be enough for an average appetite. If you try using knife and fork, you'll end up with a pool of soup on your plate; grab the dumpling by the bunched top, bite ou

spots.name: Anteb

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A family-run cafe that serves a huge variety of kebabs in a very casual cafe-type setting. The Adana and Urfa are a bargain at about 800 dram each and the Iskender, though slightly more expensive for 3,000 dram (May 2015) rivals the best. The rice pudding is pricey but tasty. Cheap drinks and free fresh hot pocket bread.

spots.name: Calumet

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Bohemian, friendly, alternative crowd. Insanely smokey (seriously). There is no outdoor section so if you're not a fan of cigarette smoke, it might not be the place for you. English speaking staff and solid drinks selection. A nice place to kill a night.

spots.name: The Club

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Has some excellent Western Armenian dishes, including manti, su borek and the amazing midia dolma. The underground space is very hip, and the tea room, when not too smoky is a good place to sit on a bean bag and chat.

spots.name: Ktoor

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Typical Armenian menu, done very well, reasonably priced, with a very large outdoor patio in front on the far end of Saryan Street. They have some ridiculously large dishes that are perfect for large groups.

spots.name: Mirzoyan Library

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Started out as a space in a traditional courtyard with a collection of photography books, it's now a café with very nice drinks and creative and excellent bites and sweets. Free wifi.

spots.name: Dolmama
spots.summary: Fusion Armenian-World cuisine. Excellent food, service and ambience. The outdoor seating out back is a way to experience the old courtyards that filled central Yerevan in the past.

spots.name: Roza

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Small bar with great ambiance in old Yerevan building, and fantastic drinks. Try the Tutovni house cocktail made with the famous local mulberry vodka.

spots.name: Jack's Pub

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Good spot for a drink, the bloody mary is legendary and the basil gin cocktail is great in the summer. You'll likely meet some repats here.

spots.name: Twelve Tables

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Very cozy spot with 12 tables, smoke-free, good menu with nice salads, soups, comfort food, and great desserts and teas. Non-smoking.

spots.name: Old Erivan

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Offers traditional food, songs, dances and the décor will make you think Disney has come to town. Almost a must for any visitor.

spots.name: Gini Pig

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Wine, beer and pizza in a small, rustic space, run by an Australian-Armenian fellow. A favorite of many for the food and vibe.

spots.name: In Vino

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The first wine bar on Saryan Street, that led the transformation of the entire neighborhood is still popular.
